After just one week of five-hour nights, a study found testosterone in young men dropped by ten to fifteen percent.
Short sleep also scrambles your hunger hormones.
Ghrelin goes up, leptin goes down.
In one study, hunger jumped about twenty-four percent, and cravings went straight to sugar and junk food.
In the gym, Daniel feels it.
Same weights, but his sets die earlier and recovery drags, because a big part of your growth hormone is released in deep sleep.
In a diet study, people sleeping five and a half hours lost the same weight as eight-and-a-half-hour sleepers,
but fifty-five percent less of it was fat. They lost more muscle instead.
Even your face shows it: paler skin, darker circles, droopier eyelids.
So if you train hard but sleep five hours, you're leaving gains on the table.
Sleep is the cheapest supplement there is.
